tldr: LightMem is a lightweight memory system for LLMs inspired by the Atkinson-Shiffrin human memory model, using three stages—sensory memory with compression and topic segmentation, topic-aware short-term memory, and offline sleep-time long-term memory updates—to dramatically reduce computational overhead while improving QA accuracy.
contributions: Introduction of LightMem, a memory system balancing performance and efficiency for LLMs in long-context and multi-turn scenarios
A cognition-inspired sensory memory module that pre-compresses inputs via LLMLingua-2 and segments by topic using attention and similarity-based boundary detection
A topic-aware short-term memory module that groups related utterances into coherent segments instead of using fixed window sizes
A sleep-time update mechanism for long-term memory that decouples expensive consolidation from online inference, enabling parallel offline updates
methods: LightMem processes interactions through three stages. First, a pre-compressing submodule uses LLMLingua-2 to filter redundant tokens based on retention probability, followed by a topic segmentation submodule that identifies boundaries as the intersection of attention-based local maxima and semantic similarity thresholds below τ. Second, topic-aware short-term memory accumulates compressed tokens in a 512-token buffer until a threshold is reached, then invokes an LLM to summarize each topic segment. Third, long-term memory inserts entries with soft (timestamped) updates at test time for low latency, then performs offline parallel updates using top-k semantic similarity retrieval with temporal constraints (only later entries update earlier ones).
results: On LONGMEMEVAL, LightMem improves QA accuracy by 2.09%-6.40% (GPT) and up to 7.67% (Qwen) over strongest baseline A-Mem. On LOCOMO, it achieves 6.10%-29.29% higher accuracy. Total token usage is reduced by up to 38× (GPT) and 20.9× (Qwen) on LONGMEMEVAL, and 20.92× (GPT) and 18.02× (Qwen) on LOCOMo. API calls are reduced by up to 30×/55.5× on LONGMEMEVAL and 39.78×/55.48× on LOCOMo. Purely online test-time costs show even larger gains: up to 106×/117× token reduction and 159×/310× fewer API calls. Runtime is accelerated by up to 12.4× (GPT) and 8.21× (Qwen). Compression ratios of 50%-80% yield comparable performance to uncompressed input.
limitations: Requires an additional model (LLMLingua-2) for pre-compression, introducing some GPU memory overhead (under 2GB reported)
Online inference is decoupled from offline consolidation, meaning long-term memory updates are not immediate but deferred to sleep periods
Evaluation is limited to two benchmarks (LONGMEMEVAL and LOCOMO), potentially limiting generalizability claims
The approach relies on the quality of LLMLingua-2 as the pre-compression model, which may not generalize equally well to all domains
